questionText: Why is RestClient preferred over RestTemplate in Spring Boot 3.2+ for synchronous HTTP communications?
optionA: RestClient offers a modern, fluent API matching WebClient while working with synchronous HttpMessageConverters without requiring reactive WebFlux dependencies.
optionB: RestTemplate throws UnsupportedOperationException in Spring Boot 3.
optionC: RestClient only communicates using binary gRPC protocols.
optionD: RestClient requires an external Netty server.
explanation: RestClient is Spring's modern synchronous HTTP client offering a fluent builder-style API, replacing RestTemplate for new development without requiring Project Reactor. (Bloom's Taxonomy Level 3: Application & Troubleshooting).

questionText: Why does internalSave() execute without transactional management when called from placeOrder()?
optionA: Direct this.internalSave() invokes the method on the target instance directly, bypassing the Spring AOP dynamic proxy interceptor chain.
optionB: @Transactional is ignored on methods named internalSave.
optionC: Spring Boot disables transactions inside Service classes by default.
optionD: The transaction is rolled back before entering the method.
explanation: Spring AOP advice is applied through proxy objects. Internal this.method() calls bypass the proxy wrapper. To fix: inject the proxy self-reference, use AspectJ compile-time weaving, or refactor to another bean. (Bloom's Taxonomy Level 3: Application & Troubleshooting).

questionText: Under default Spring @Transactional configuration, why does throwing a checked exception NOT trigger a transaction rollback?
optionA: Spring Declarative Transactions roll back on unchecked exceptions (RuntimeException and Error) by default unless rollbackFor is configured.
optionB: Checked exceptions are silently committed by database drivers.
optionC: Spring Boot transactions only roll back on OutOfMemoryError.
optionD: The database automatically catches custom checked exceptions.
explanation: By default, Spring transactions roll back only on unchecked exceptions. To roll back on checked exceptions, declare @Transactional(rollbackFor = Exception.class). (Bloom's Taxonomy Level 3: Application & Troubleshooting).

questionText: How does @EntityGraph prevent N+1 queries when loading Department entities with lazy-loaded employees?
optionA: It generates a single SQL query with an INNER/LEFT JOIN to eagerly fetch the specified associated employees in a single round-trip.
optionB: It stores all Department records in Redis cache.
optionC: It disables lazy loading across all entities in the entire JVM.
optionD: It forces the database to execute background stored procedures.
explanation: @EntityGraph allows overriding default fetch plans on a per-query basis, instructing JPA/Hibernate to use a SQL JOIN to fetch child relationships in a single query. (Bloom's Taxonomy Level 3: Application & Troubleshooting).

questionText: What is the core function of customJwtConverter in this Spring Security configuration?
optionA: It extracts customized claims (such as realm_access.roles) from the validated JWT token and maps them into GrantedAuthority objects in the SecurityContext.
optionB: It decrypts the incoming TLS TCP socket traffic.
optionC: It generates asymmetric RSA keys for every HTTP request.
optionD: It stores the user password in plaintext in session memory.
explanation: JwtAuthenticationConverter transforms JWT payload claims into Spring Security GrantedAuthority instances (e.g. ROLE_ADMIN), enabling method security annotations like @PreAuthorize. (Bloom's Taxonomy Level 3: Application & Troubleshooting).

questionText: How does Micrometer Tracing maintain end-to-end trace correlation across downstream microservices?
optionA: By automatically injecting W3C Trace Context headers ('traceparent' and 'tracestate') into outgoing HTTP request headers via client interceptors.
optionB: By writing trace IDs to a central database on every HTTP request.
optionC: By broadcasting UDP heartbeat packets to all network switches.
optionD: By attaching trace IDs to the TCP handshake SYN packet.
explanation: Micrometer Tracing injects standard W3C Trace Context HTTP headers (traceparent) into downstream requests, enabling distributed tracing across microservices. (Bloom's Taxonomy Level 3: Application & Troubleshooting).

questionText: When 6 out of 10 requests fail in the sliding window, what immediate behavior change occurs for the 11th request?

resilience4j.circuitbreaker.instances.paymentService.sliding-window-size=10

questionText: What is the purpose of dynamic request(n) signaling in Reactive Streams backpressure?
optionA: It allows the consumer to pull only the number of items it has capacity to process, preventing producer fast-push memory overflow.
optionB: It forces the publisher to run in a single thread.
optionC: It converts asynchronous streams into blocking JDBC queries.
optionD: It pauses the OS CPU clock until data arrives.

optionB: It forces the publisher to run in a single thread.
optionC: It converts asynchronous streams into blocking JDBC queries.
optionD: It pauses the OS CPU clock until data arrives.
explanation: Backpressure in Reactive Streams (Project Reactor) allows subscribers to regulate data flow by demanding specific batch sizes via request(n), preventing buffer overflows. (Bloom's Taxonomy Level 3: Application & Troubleshooting).

questionText: Why is RestClient preferred over RestTemplate in Spring Boot 3.2+ for synchronous HTTP communications?
optionA: RestClient offers a modern, fluent API matching WebClient while working with synchronous HttpMessageConverters without requiring reactive WebFlux dependencies.
optionB: RestTemplate throws UnsupportedOperationException in Spring Boot 3.
optionC: RestClient only communicates using binary gRPC protocols.
optionD: RestClient requires an external Netty server.

questionText: Why does internalSave() execute without transactional management when called from placeOrder()?
optionA: Direct this.internalSave() invokes the method on the target instance directly, bypassing the Spring AOP dynamic proxy interceptor chain.
optionB: @Transactional is ignored on methods named internalSave.
optionC: Spring Boot disables transactions inside Service classes by default.
optionD: The transaction is rolled back before entering the method.
explanation: Spring AOP advice is applied through proxy objects. Internal this.method() calls bypass the proxy wrapper. To fix: inject the proxy self-reference, use AspectJ compile-time weaving, or refactor to another bean. (Bloom's Taxonomy Level 3: Application & Troubleshooting).

questionText: Under default Spring @Transactional configuration, why does throwing a checked exception NOT trigger a transaction rollback?
optionA: Spring Declarative Transactions roll back on unchecked exceptions (RuntimeException and Error) by default unless rollbackFor is configured.
optionB: Checked exceptions are silently committed by database drivers.
optionC: Spring Boot transactions only roll back on OutOfMemoryError.
optionD: The database automatically catches custom checked exceptions.
explanation: By default, Spring transactions roll back only on unchecked exceptions. To roll back on checked exceptions, declare @Transactional(rollbackFor = Exception.class). (Bloom's Taxonomy Level 3: Application & Troubleshooting).

questionText: How does @EntityGraph prevent N+1 queries when loading Department entities with lazy-loaded employees?
optionA: It generates a single SQL query with an INNER/LEFT JOIN to eagerly fetch the specified associated employees in a single round-trip.
optionB: It stores all Department records in Redis cache.
optionC: It disables lazy loading across all entities in the entire JVM.
optionD: It forces the database to execute background stored procedures.
explanation: @EntityGraph allows overriding default fetch plans on a per-query basis, instructing JPA/Hibernate to use a SQL JOIN to fetch child relationships in a single query. (Bloom's Taxonomy Level 3: Application & Troubleshooting).

questionText: What is the core function of customJwtConverter in this Spring Security configuration?
optionA: It extracts customized claims (such as realm_access.roles) from the validated JWT token and maps them into GrantedAuthority objects in the SecurityContext.
optionB: It decrypts the incoming TLS TCP socket traffic.
optionC: It generates asymmetric RSA keys for every HTTP request.
optionD: It stores the user password in plaintext in session memory.
explanation: JwtAuthenticationConverter transforms JWT payload claims into Spring Security GrantedAuthority instances (e.g. ROLE_ADMIN), enabling method security annotations like @PreAuthorize. (Bloom's Taxonomy Level 3: Application & Troubleshooting).

questionText: How does Micrometer Tracing maintain end-to-end trace correlation across downstream microservices?
optionA: By automatically injecting W3C Trace Context headers ('traceparent' and 'tracestate') into outgoing HTTP request headers via client interceptors.
optionB: By writing trace IDs to a central database on every HTTP request.
optionC: By broadcasting UDP heartbeat packets to all network switches.
optionD: By attaching trace IDs to the TCP handshake SYN packet.
explanation: Micrometer Tracing injects standard W3C Trace Context HTTP headers (traceparent) into downstream requests, enabling distributed tracing across microservices. (Bloom's Taxonomy Level 3: Application & Troubleshooting).
